title: Matar Paneer
subtitle: Indian peas and paneer in a spiced tomato sauce
excerpt: Matar paneer is a simple North Indian curry of peas and fresh cheese in a lightly spiced tomato sauce. It is one of the quickest curries to put together and works well as a weeknight main or a side in a larger spread. Frozen peas are ideal here.
sourceNotes: Matar paneer is a classic of North Indian vegetarian cooking, popular across Punjab, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh. It is one of the most straightforward paneer dishes and a natural companion to dal and rice or chapati.

content.text: Fry the paneer until golden before adding it to the sauce -- this stops it breaking apart during cooking. If you cannot find paneer, halloumi is the closest substitute.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide frying pan over medium-high heat. Fry the paneer cubes for 2 minutes per side until golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the pan. Add the cumin seeds. When they sizzle, add the onion. Cook for 7 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the turmeric and coriander and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tinned tomatoes and salt. Cook for 6 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Add the frozen peas. Cook for 3 minutes. Return the paneer to the pan. Stir gently.
Add the garam masala. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with rice or roti.

items.symptom: Paneer breaking up in the sauce
items.cause: Not fried first, or fried but handled too roughly
items.fix: Pre-fry the paneer and stir very gently when adding back to the sauce

items.cause: Tinned tomatoes not cooked long enough
items.fix: Cook the tomato sauce for 2 extra minutes and add a pinch of sugar if needed

items.cause: Added too early or cooked too long
items.fix: Add frozen peas directly from the freezer 3 minutes before the end -- they only need gentle heating

content.text: Matar paneer is everyday vegetarian food across North India. It is a standard item in dhabas and home kitchens. The dish is mild enough to serve to children and substantial enough to work as a main course. It is almost always eaten with flatbread or rice, as part of a larger meal.
